title: Strength + Mobility
notes: Hello Rick! Please try these exercises for about 4 weeks. I have only put a few exercises so it doesn't take up much time. The exercises are designed to work on strength and mobility between our sessions. Please complete the Workout Check-in at the end of your workout and ask questions if you need clarification anytime. You can do this workout 2x/week. Enjoy! Colleen~

warmup.name: Arm Swings
warmup.cues: Relax shoulders, ribs down, tall spine

warmup.name: Torso Twists
warmup.cues: Rotate through upper back, hips mostly forward

warmup.name: Inchworms
warmup.cues: Slow and controlled. Hinge at hips, crawl out to straight-arm plank and back.

warmup.name: Wall Angels
warmup.cues: Stand with back flat against wall. Slide arms up and down in Y-T-W pattern.

primary.name: Wall Push-Ups
primary.cues: Engage core before beginning. Hands below shoulder height. Bend elbows and let body weight move toward wall — even one inch at a time. No pain only.
primary.progression: Move closer to wall to make easier. Move feet back as you improve

primary.name: Scapular Push-Ups
primary.cues: Hold a straight-arm plank. Press shoulders away from ears — spread shoulder blades apart (protraction). Then let go and squeeze shoulder blades together (retraction). Repeat with control.
primary.progression: Progress to full push-up range when scapular control is strong

primary.name: Front Raises
primary.cues: Stand tall, ribs down. Soft bend in elbows. Raise arms straight in front. Stop before shoulder height. Lower slowly.
primary.progression: Increase range only when pain-free. Stay below your pain threshold

primary.name: Lateral Arm Raises
primary.cues: Stand tall, ribs down. Soft bend in elbows. Lift arms out to the side toward shoulder height. Lower slowly with control.
primary.progression: Add very light weight only when fully pain-free at shoulder height

warmup.name: Hip Openers
warmup.cues: Relax shoulders, ribs down, tall spine

warmup.name: High Knees
warmup.cues: Drive knee to hip height. Stay tall. Increase speed only if posture stays controlled.

warmup.name: Air Squats
warmup.cues: Keep your weight on your heels and your chin and chest up looking straight ahead to keep your posture.
warmup.contraindications: If you feel pain in your knees, try not to go as low.
warmup.progression: if it is too difficult, try doing a wall sit instead.

warmup.name: Step Back Lunges
warmup.cues: Step back softly. Front heel grounded. Torso tall. Control the return.

primary.name: Bosu Step Ups
primary.cues:
Stand tall, with good posture.
Step to the very top of the Bosu - with your whole foot.
primary.contraindications: If you are recovering from injury, start slowly and use a counter/bar if needed.
primary.progression: If you feel knee, ankle or foot pain, move off the Bosu. If you want to increase intensity, run up and down instead of step-ups.

primary.name: Single-Leg Deadlift
primary.cues: Hinge from hip. Maintain long spine. Working leg soft.

primary.name: Weighted Single-Leg Torso Twists
primary.cues: Always turn toward the knee that is up. If you cannot keep form without touching the floor, just tap the floor between reps.

primary.name: Wall Sit with Pilates Ball
primary.cues: Make sure you press your bodyweight into the wall and your knees stay behind your toes. Squeeze the ball to activate your adductors. Try a 10 second hold at the end to feel the muscle work in an isometric hold.
primary.coachingFocus: Stability for adductors and isometric for quads and glutes
primary.contraindications: If you have knee pain, try not to bend as far down, or get a larger ball to avoid inner knee pain.
primary.progression: Add weight for progression, remove ball for regression

primary.name: DB Calf Raises
primary.cues: Keep your arms relaxed and shoulders down, with your core engaged, standing tall.
primary.contraindications: If you feel pain please stop.
primary.progression: Try without weights and if you need to hold onto something to keep your posture, it is better than leaning to one side.
primary.startWeight: You do not have to use weight here. Also, try single-leg calf raises but keep posture tall with fingertips on a counter.

warmup.name: Torso Twists
warmup.cues: Rotate through upper back, hips mostly forward

warmup.name: Weighted Side Bends
warmup.cues: Hold a kettlebell in each hand, stand tall. Alternate leaning as far as you can to each side. Pause between sides to reset posture. Core stays engaged.
warmup.progression: Increase weight when full range is controlled with good posture
warmup.startWeight: You don't have to use weight, but if you do - use 10lbs or just go slowly when you move to stretch from the hip to ribs.

primary.name: Band Lat Pulldowns
primary.cues: Make sure the band is tight at shoulder-width apart, pull hands away as you pull down - on an angle toward your chin, not straight down.
primary.contraindications: Don't do this if you have trouble holding shoulders above head.

primary.name: Reverse Flys
primary.cues: Arms straight in front. Pull back, widen hands, squeeze elbows behind to activate upper back.
primary.startWeight: 8-10lbs or just go slowly and hold at the top, squeezing your elbows toward your spine, and your arms away from the midline of your body.

primary.name: Robots
primary.cues: Keep arms low to start. Palms facing outward. Keep elbows at comfortable level as you turn palms down. NO pain. Stay low and work slow.
primary.progression: Goal image is the end point — not the starting point. Progress gradually
